examDifficulty.heading: Is the OmniStudio Consultant Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The OmniStudio Consultant exam is moderately difficult. It rewards practical Salesforce experience because many questions ask you to choose the best configuration, design, or troubleshooting approach rather than recall isolated definitions.
bullets: ~65% passing score — build a margin above the minimum before booking.
Scenario-based choices — expect questions that test when to use OmniScript, DataRaptor, or FlexCards.
Hands-on context matters — candidates who have configured or supported OmniStudio in a real org are better prepared than candidates who only memorize notes.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Aim for 75%+ on timed practice sets before booking. If your score is below that, review the highest-weight topics first and retake questions until you can explain why each wrong option is wrong.

examFormat.heading: OmniStudio Consultant Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The OmniStudio Consultant exam is a timed Salesforce credential exam. Use the format below to plan pacing and practice-test strategy.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: A meaningful share of questions are scenario-based. The common pattern is a business requirement followed by several plausible Salesforce options; your job is to identify the safest, most maintainable choice for OmniStudio.
bestWayToPass: Start with the official outline: Map each exam objective to your notes, Trailhead practice, and weak areas before taking full mocks.
Prioritize high-impact topics: Spend extra time on OmniScript, DataRaptor, and FlexCards because these usually drive the hardest scenario questions.
Practice under time pressure: Use timed question sets so you learn when to move on and return to marked questions later.
Review explanations deeply: Do not just memorize the right option; write down why the other options are less appropriate for the scenario.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers solution design with OmniStudio tools -- selecting the right mix of FlexCards, OmniScripts, DataRaptors, and Integration Procedures to build scalable guided experiences for Industry Cloud implementations.

keyConcepts.h2: OmniStudio Consultant: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: FlexCards: Displaying Data Contextually
blocks.body: FlexCards display contextual information from Salesforce records or external data sources on a card-style UI. They can be embedded in Experience Cloud pages, Lightning record pages, or other OmniStudio components. Child FlexCards show related record data. Custom actions on FlexCards trigger OmniScripts, open Lightning components, or navigate to records. Data sources: Salesforce **SOQL** (DataRaptor Extract), Integration Procedures, or **Apex**. The consultant designs FlexCards to surface the right information in the right context — reducing the need for users to navigate away to find related data.

blocks.heading: OmniScripts: Guided User Experiences
blocks.body: OmniScripts create guided, multi-step processes for users — similar to a wizard. Steps and groups organise the experience. Elements: Text Input, Select (dropdown), Date Picker, Checkbox, Lookup, Navigation (radio buttons), Formula, and more. Conditional display rules show or hide elements based on prior responses. Data sources populate dropdown options and pre-fill fields. Custom **validation rules** enforce business rules before moving to the next step. The consultant designs OmniScripts for complex data entry processes like customer onboarding, service requests, or insurance claims.

blocks.heading: Integration Procedures: Backend Orchestration
blocks.body: Integration Procedures (IPs) orchestrate backend calls without user interaction — they are called by OmniScripts, FlexCards, or other automated processes. Actions within an IP: DataRaptor Extract (query Salesforce), DataRaptor Load (write to Salesforce), HTTP Action (call external **REST API**), **Apex** Action (call custom Apex), Set Values (assign variables). IPs support conditional branching and looping. The consultant designs IPs to aggregate data from multiple sources, transform it, and return structured results — keeping business logic out of the UI layer.

blocks.heading: DataRaptors: Data Access and Transformation
blocks.body: DataRaptors are data transformation tools with four types: Extract (read from Salesforce — returns a structured JSON), Load (write to Salesforce — creates or updates records), Transform (map and reshape data between structures without touching Salesforce), Turbo Extract (high-performance read for simple queries using **SOQL**). DataRaptor Extract replaces SOQL in OmniStudio components. Load handles parent-child record creation in a single operation. The consultant selects the appropriate DataRaptor type based on whether the operation reads, writes, or transforms data.

blocks.heading: OmniStudio Architecture in Industry Clouds
blocks.body: OmniStudio is the foundation for Salesforce Industry Clouds (Health Cloud, Financial Services Cloud, Communications Cloud, Energy & Utilities). Industry-specific FlexCards and OmniScripts come pre-built with the industry cloud packages — the consultant configures and extends them rather than building from scratch. OmniStudio components integrate with Salesforce standard objects and industry-specific data models. Business Rules Engine (BRE) provides declarative if-then rules that drive OmniScript branching without hard-coding logic. The consultant understands how OmniStudio connects to the broader industry cloud architecture.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce OmniStudio Consultant Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The OmniStudio Consultant exam tests solution design and business requirements analysis for OmniStudio implementations. Focus on choosing the right OmniStudio tool for each business scenario and designing scalable configurations.

blocks.heading: Tool Selection Framework
blocks.body: Know when to use each OmniStudio tool: FlexCards for contextual data display, OmniScripts for guided user processes, DataRaptors for Salesforce data integration, and Integration Procedures for complex orchestration.

blocks.heading: Business Process to OmniScript Mapping
blocks.body: Know how to decompose a business process into OmniScript steps, identify reusable components, and design the data flow between steps. Understand when sub-OmniScripts improve reusability.

blocks.heading: Data Integration Architecture
blocks.body: Know when to use DataRaptor Extract vs. Integration Procedure for data retrieval, how to handle complex data transformations, and when to call external APIs from Integration Procedures.

blocks.heading: FlexCard Use Cases
blocks.body: Know common FlexCard use cases: account/contact dashboards, case summaries, 360-degree customer views. Understand how FlexCard states manage different data scenarios (loading, empty, error, data).

blocks.heading: Performance & Scalability
blocks.body: Know best practices for OmniStudio performance: minimizing DataRaptor steps, using Turbo Extract for simple reads, caching Integration Procedure results, and structuring OmniScripts to minimize server calls.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the primary focus of an OmniStudio Consultant?
options: Designing and implementing solutions using OmniStudio tools that are sustainable, scalable, and meet customer business requirements
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniStudio Consultants design and implement OmniStudio solutions that are sustainable, scalable, and meet business requirements.

sampleQuestions.question: Which OmniStudio tool is used for guided, step-by-step experiences?
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniScript provides guided, step-by-step digital experiences.

sampleQuestions.question: What should an OmniStudio Consultant ensure for long-term success?
options: Sustainable and scalable design that contributes to long-term customer success
sampleQuestions.explanation: Consultants ensure solutions are sustainable, scalable, and contribute to long-term success.

sampleQuestions.question: Which industries commonly use OmniStudio?
options: Financial Services, Insurance, and other industries
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniStudio is used in Financial Services, Insurance, and other industries for digital flows.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a FlexCard used for?
options: Displaying compact, card-based views of record data
sampleQuestions.explanation: FlexCards display compact, card-based views of data with declarative layout.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a DataRaptor used for in OmniStudio?
options: To extract, load, or transform data (DEXT, DMLT, etc.)
sampleQuestions.explanation: DataRaptors handle data extract, load, and transform operations.

sampleQuestions.question: Which OmniStudio component invokes Apex or external services?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Integration Procedures call Apex and external systems.

sampleQuestions.question: What does OmniScript validation support?
options: Required fields, custom validation, and conditional rules
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniScript supports required, custom, and conditional validation.

sampleQuestions.question: Which deployment method is used for OmniStudio artifacts?
sampleQuestions.explanation: FlexDeploy and source-driven deployment manage OmniStudio artifacts.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of OmniScript elements?
options: To define steps, fields, and actions in the OmniScript flow
sampleQuestions.explanation: Elements define the structure and behavior of OmniScript steps.

sampleQuestions.question: Which OmniStudio feature supports conditional display?
options: Conditional visibility and branching based on data or user input
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniScript supports conditional visibility and branching.

sampleQuestions.question: What does an OmniStudio Consultant ensure for scalability?
options: Reusable elements, efficient DataRaptors, and governance
sampleQuestions.explanation: Reusable design and efficient DataRaptors support scalability.

sampleQuestions.question: Which OmniStudio artifact can be embedded in Lightning pages?
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniScript and FlexCards can be embedded in Lightning pages.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the benefit of OmniScript over custom Apex UI?
options: Declarative, faster to build, and easier to maintain for guided flows
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniScript is declarative and faster to build for guided flows.

sampleQuestions.question: Which industry use case is common for OmniStudio?
options: Quote-to-cash, onboarding, and service workflows in Financial Services
sampleQuestions.explanation: Financial Services uses OmniStudio for quote-to-cash and onboarding.
